# vss -- command reference

<!-- GENERATED by tools/build_manual_reference.py. Do not edit by hand:
     change the parser, the timer or the tool's tables, then run
     .venv/bin/python tools/build_manual_reference.py > docs/REFERENCE.md
     tests/test_manual_reference.py holds this file equal to the code. -->

Every command, every flag, what it reads, writes, calls and sends. The flags are read off the argument parsers and the timers off `deploy/`, and a test fails when this page and the code differ. How to *use* the commands is in [the manual](MANUAL.md).

Run everything from the repository root:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m vss <command> [flags]
.venv/bin/python tools/<tool>.py [flags]
```

## What a command may touch

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `read-only` | prints; writes no file and sends nothing |
| `local` | writes under `data/` or `reports/` -- regenerable, gitignored |
| `record` | writes under `config/`, `reference/` or `sources/` -- the record, tracked in git; a backup is taken first where a file is replaced |
| `watchlist` | may write `config/watchlist.yaml` |
| `sends` | may POST to ntfy, i.e. reach the owner's phone |

A command carries every class that applies to any of its forms. **Changes nothing** names the form that writes no file and sends nothing; where a command has none, the row says so.

Unless a command's table says otherwise its exit codes are: `0` completed; `2` the watchlist or a configuration file is missing or malformed; `130` interrupted.

## The `vss` commands

### `vss run`

The nightly report: fetch prices, apply the staleness gate, print every verdict.

> fetch, evaluate and report the watchlist.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the report but write nothing: no report file, no cache, no database |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist instead of config/watchlist.yaml |
| `--ticker X` | restrict the run to a single ticker from the watchlist |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; `data/cache/` where a fetch fails; the newest stored ranking (the E97 ranked watch); `data/refresh_state.json` |
| **Writes** | `reports/<date>.md` (`reports/<date>.<TICKER>.md` with `--ticker`); `data/vss.sqlite`; `data/cache/`; `data/pricewatch_state.json`; `data/block_push_state.json`; `reports/OVERVIEW.html` after a full run |
| **Network** | Yahoo (yfinance) daily prices; ntfy |
| **Sends** | to `NTFY_TOPIC`: the NEEDS OWNER pointer (E92), a ranked-watch crossing (E97), every HELD or MBP name blocked on a stale close, and the dead man's switch's gap line |
| **Exit codes** | `0` completed -- a ticker that errored is an ERROR row, not a failure; `1` coverage short: too few names were priced, the run does not reset the staleness clock and no healthcheck ping goes; `2` the watchlist is missing or malformed, or `--ticker` is not on it; `3` a `--dry-run` REFUSED because a HELD name or one with an MBP has a close more than one session old (no trigger was checked, so no report is printed); `130` interrupted |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss run --dry-run` (it still fetches prices, and the vendor library keeps its own cache under `data/yf-cache/`) |

### `vss earnings`

Read one primary-source report and test it against the hard kills (section 4.2).

> read a primary-source report and flag FRAMEWORK 4.2 trips.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | any ticker from the watchlist, whatever its status (REQUIRED) |
| `--url URL` | primary source: company IR release or filing. NEVER a news article (one of these is required: `--text-file PATH`) |
| `--text-file PATH` | a locally saved primary source: text, HTML or a downloaded PDF (one of these is required: `--url URL`) |
| `--shadow / --no-shadow` | log to sqlite and send nothing (default: on) |
| `--period YYYY-Qn` | extract this period, reading it from a comparative column if the document is about another quarter |
| `--compare` | read the source twice and null any field the two runs disagree on |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; the URL or the file given |
| **Writes** | `data/vss.sqlite` (table `earnings_runs`). Never `quarters:` -- the figures are PROPOSED in the alert as a YAML block |
| **Network** | the source URL; OpenRouter (the extraction model) |
| **Sends** | nothing, with or without `--shadow` |
| **Exit codes** | `0` read; `1` the source could not be fetched or read; `2` watchlist error |

### `vss xbrl`

A US filer's tagged figures straight from SEC; `--annual --write` fills a store.

> pull a US filer's tagged facts from SEC XBRL -- no HTML, no PDF.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | any ticker from the watchlist, whatever its status (REQUIRED) |
| `--cik N` | override the watchlist's cik for this run |
| `--limit N` | how many recent periods to pull (default: 8 quarters, or 5 years with --annual) |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |
| `--annual` | fetch the ANNUAL facts section 5 needs -- cash flow, capex, share count and net debt -- and emit config/manual/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml. Filers stopped tagging discrete fourth quarters in 2021, so the quarter shape cannot reach a current twelve-month basis and this can |
| `--write` | with --annual: write config/manual/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml. Refuses a file of any other origin -- a history mixing whole units with millions is a history in which no comparison means anything |
| `--force` | with --write: replace a file this path itself wrote, backing it up first. Discards every VERIFIED flag it holds. It does NOT open the mixed-origin refusal |
| `--manual-dir PATH` | write into an alternate directory instead of config/manual |
| `--quote-currency CCY` | INTAKE only -- the listing currency of a ticker that is NOT on the watchlist. Entering a name on the watchlist stamps dd_at_entry and freezes Gate 1 (E12), so a candidate is read BEFORE it is entered; the quote currency is a fact about a LISTING and not a tagged fact, so it is stated here or the intake refuses |
| `--e140-fill` | E140 / E140.1: put `working_capital_change` and `acquisitions_paid` into each fiscal year an EXISTING sec-xbrl store holds, and its `roll_forward:` block (the latest 10-Q). Nothing else in the file moves. Prints what it would write; --write writes it, backing the old file up |
| `--name NAME` | INTAKE only -- override the filer name. Left out, the SEC's own `entityName` is used, which is the filer's own |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml` (the `cik:`); with `--e140-fill` the existing store |
| **Writes** | every form logs its run in `data/vss.sqlite`; no store is touched without `--write`. With `--annual --write`: `config/manual/<TICKER>.yaml`. With `--e140-fill --write`: two fields per year and `roll_forward:` in that store, the old file backed up |
| **Network** | `data.sec.gov` (needs `VSS_SEC_CONTACT`) |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` fetched; `1` SEC could not be read or the write was refused; `2` watchlist error, or `--write` without `--annual` |
| **Changes nothing** | none strictly: the run is logged. Without `--write` no store and no record is touched |

### `vss manual`

Validate a store and say whether section 5 may read it; merge a draft into it.

> validate a hand-entered fundamentals file and gate section 5 on it.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the ticker whose file to read: config/manual/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml (REQUIRED) |
| `--asof YYYY-MM-DD` | the date the accounts are judged against, so STALE is reproducible (default: today) |
| `--dir PATH` | read from an alternate directory instead of config/manual |
| `--merge-draft` | merge config/manual/drafts/&lt;TICKER&gt;.&lt;origin&gt;.yaml into the store: adds what it lacks, never overwrites, prints conflicts; backup first |
| `--origin esef-ixbrl|llm-pdf` | which draft --merge-draft takes (default esef-ixbrl) |
| `--dry-run` | with --merge-draft: report, write nothing |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/manual/<TICKER>.yaml`; with `--merge-draft` also `config/manual/drafts/<TICKER>.<origin>.yaml` |
| **Writes** | nothing. With `--merge-draft` (and no `--dry-run`): the store, the old file backed up to `arkiv/config-bak/` |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` the store loads and section 5 may read it; `1` section 5 REFUSES (an UNVERIFIED figure, a stale file, legs from two periods); `2` the file is malformed |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss manual --ticker X`; `--merge-draft --dry-run` |

### `vss pdfdraft`

A model reads a report's statement pages twice into a DRAFT, never the store.

> a model reads a report's statement pages (twice) and gated figures become config/manual/drafts/&lt;TICKER&gt;.llm-pdf.yaml (UNVERIFIED; E149).

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the ticker the draft is for (REQUIRED) |
| `--pdf PATH` | the report under sources/ (REQUIRED) |
| `--period YYYY-Qn|YYYY-FY` | the target period: its column and nothing else (REQUIRED) |
| `--currency CURRENCY` | reporting currency (default: the live store's) |
| `--write` | write the draft and its run record |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the PDF under `sources/`; the live store (its currency) |
| **Writes** | nothing without `--write`. With it: `config/manual/drafts/<TICKER>.llm-pdf.yaml` and its run record. Never the live store |
| **Network** | OpenRouter (the model reads the statement pages twice) |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` read; `2` no `--currency` and no live store to take it from |
| **Changes nothing** | without `--write` (the model is still called) |

### `vss esef`

Read a Nordic issuer's ESEF report packages; `--draft` writes a DRAFT.

> read a Nordic issuer's ESEF report packages in sources/ and, with --draft, write config/manual/drafts/&lt;TICKER&gt;.esef-ixbrl.yaml.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the ticker whose packages under sources/ to read (REQUIRED) |
| `--draft` | write the draft (every figure UNVERIFIED; merge it with `vss manual --merge-draft`) |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the ESEF report packages (`.zip`) under `sources/`; `config/mfn_entities.yaml` (the LEI) |
| **Writes** | nothing without `--draft`. With it: `config/manual/drafts/<TICKER>.esef-ixbrl.yaml`. Never the live store |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` read; `1` no readable package in `sources/` |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss esef --ticker X` |

### `vss appendix`

Read an issuer's figures workbook (xlsx) through a committed cell map.

> read an issuer's figures appendix (xlsx) through a committed cell map and emit a filled config/manual/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the ticker whose map to use: config/manual/maps/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml (REQUIRED) |
| `--xlsx PATH` | the appendix workbook, normally one that `vss nordic` downloaded into sources/ (REQUIRED) |
| `--write` | write config/manual/&lt;TICKER&gt;.yaml. Refuses when the file exists: overwriting would reset every VERIFIED figure in it |
| `--force` | with --write: replace an existing file, backing it up first. Discards every VERIFIED flag it holds |
| `--maps-dir PATH` | alternate map directory |
| `--manual-dir PATH` | alternate output directory |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the workbook; `config/manual/maps/<TICKER>.yaml` |
| **Writes** | nothing without `--write`. With it: `config/manual/<TICKER>.yaml` -- refused where the file exists unless `--force`, which backs it up first |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` emitted; `1` the emitted file does not validate; `2` the map is missing or a label does not match |
| **Changes nothing** | without `--write` |

### `vss nordic`

List and download reports from the Nordic exchange feed (Oslo: NewsWeb).

> list and download report documents from the Nordic exchange's own disclosure feed. Downloads and records; reads nothing.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the ticker, as config/nordic_issuers.yaml keys it (REQUIRED) |
| `--resolve TEXT` | search the feed for this text and show the (market, company) candidates for --ticker. The service has no company directory, so the mapping is established once and stored |
| `--write` | with --resolve: append the top candidate to config/nordic_issuers.yaml. Backs the file up first and never replaces an existing entry |
| `--download ID` | download the document of this disclosure id |
| `--attachment N` | which file of the disclosure. Required when it carries more than one -- never guessed |
| `--period YYYY-Qn` | MANUAL, and required to download: the fiscal period the document COVERS. YYYY-Qn, YYYY-H1, YYYY-H2 or YYYY-FY |
| `--reports` | show only report categories. The category is the issuer's filing choice, so this HIDES real reports; the count hidden is printed |
| `--language XX` | restrict to one language edition, e.g. en. Defaults to the issuer's stored preference |
| `--limit N` | rows per page (the service caps at 200) |
| `--start N` | first row of the window. Pagination is start, not offset -- offset is accepted and ignored |
| `--sources-dir PATH` | where documents and the manifest go (default: sources) |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/nordic_issuers.yaml` (`config/oslo_issuers.yaml` for a `.OL` ticker); `sources/manifest.json` |
| **Writes** | nothing when listing. With `--download`: the document under `sources/` and its `sources/manifest.json` entry. With `--resolve --write`: the issuer file, backed up first |
| **Network** | the Nasdaq Nordic disclosure feed; Euronext Oslo NewsWeb for `.OL` |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` done; `1` `--resolve` found no candidate |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss nordic --ticker X` and `--reports` (a listing) |

### `vss watch`

Tell the phone when a watched name files a report, a guidance change or a warning.

> check the WATCH-PRICED, WATCH-GATED and PIPELINE names for new periodic reports, guidance changes and profit warnings, and notify via ntfy.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--state PATH` | where the cursor is kept (default: data/watch_state.json). NOT the watchlist: a cursor is not a decision |
| `--no-send` | check and print, POST nothing. The state file is still advanced |
| `--ntfy-url URL` | override the topic URL (default: the VSS_NTFY_URL environment variable) |
| `--cron` | print the crontab line to add BY HAND and exit. This command installs nothing |
| `--sec-only` | ask EDGAR only: the SEC arm, which covers every watched US filer with a `cik:` and passes 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K ITEM 2.02 (the earnings release, which arrives before the 10-Q). NOTIFY ONLY -- it never writes the store or the watchlist (not together with `--nordic-only`) |
| `--nordic-only` | ask the Nasdaq Nordic feed only. Without either flag BOTH arms run, each reporting the names it covers (not together with `--sec-only`) |
| `--read` | SEC arm: read each passed filing through `vss earnings` IN SHADOW (read twice, compared), writing the alert to data/autoread/ and SENDING IT NOWHERE. Runs after the notification, so it cannot cost it |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; `config/nordic_issuers.yaml`; `data/watch_state.json` |
| **Writes** | `data/watch_state.json` -- the cursor is advanced EVEN WITH `--no-send`; with `--read` also `data/autoread/` |
| **Network** | the Nasdaq Nordic feed; EDGAR (`data.sec.gov`); ntfy; with `--read` OpenRouter |
| **Sends** | to `VSS_NTFY_URL`: a new periodic report, a guidance change or a profit warning on a watched name. `--no-send` prints instead |
| **Exit codes** | `0` |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss watch --cron` only (prints a crontab line). `--no-send` sends nothing but still moves the cursor, so the next real run will not repeat what it showed |

### `vss refresh`

On a name's report date: fetch the filing, fill the store, write a report (E92).

> E92: fetch a name's filing on its catalyst date, extract into the store and write reports/REFRESH-&lt;TICKER&gt;-&lt;date&gt;.md. It NEVER writes fv_base, tier, mbp, stop or status, and NEVER scores a gate.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | one ticker from the watchlist (one of these is required: `--due`) |
| `--due` | every watchlist name whose catalyst date has passed and whose store holds no data for the period that catalyst reports on (one of these is required: `--ticker X`) |
| `--dry-run` | say what would be fetched and from where; fetch nothing, write no store entry, no report and no state |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |
| `--manual-dir PATH` | read and write stores in an alternate directory instead of config/manual |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; the stores; `data/refresh_state.json` |
| **Writes** | the name's store under `config/manual/` (UNVERIFIED figures); `reports/REFRESH-<TICKER>-<date>.md`; `data/refresh_state.json`. Never `fv_base`, `tier`, `mbp`, `stop_price` or `status` |
| **Network** | EDGAR; the Nordic feeds; OpenRouter |
| **Sends** | nothing itself; the nightly `vss run` sends the NEEDS OWNER pointer for what a refresh left waiting |
| **Exit codes** | `0` |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss refresh --due --dry-run` |

### `vss doctor`

Can this machine run vss? Checks the install, the settings and the timers.

> read-only: can this machine run vss? python, imports, the SEC contact, vss.env's mode, ntfy, the database's tables, the snapshots, the timers, the checkout path. Exit 0 or 1.

No arguments.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the Python environment; `~/.config/vss/vss.env` (mode and owner); `data/vss.sqlite` opened read-only; the newest snapshot; the user-level systemd timers (enabled, active); the units' `WorkingDirectory` |
| **Writes** | nothing |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` every check passed or only warned; `1` any FAIL |
| **Changes nothing** | always |

### `vss sales`

Every closed position against the indices since its sale; reconcile fills (E165).

> every closed position against OMXS30 and the S&P 500 from its own sale date, plus fixed 30/90/365-day marks (FRAMEWORK-EDITS B45). Reads the watchlist's sales: blocks; a fill with no price is DATA MISSING, never read off a bar.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the record but write no report file and no price cache |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |
| `--reconcile EXPORT_CSV` | E165: match every sell row of an Avanza transaction export against the booked fills, write config/sales_reconciled.yaml, print the differences; exit 1 on any. Reads no prices |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | with --reconcile: the first date reconciled (default: the earliest booked fill) |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the `sales:` blocks in `config/watchlist.yaml`; with `--reconcile` the account export CSV |
| **Writes** | `reports/SALES-RECORD-<date>.md` and `data/cache/`. With `--reconcile`: `config/sales_reconciled.yaml`, and no prices are read |
| **Network** | Yahoo (prices and the two indices); none with `--reconcile` |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0`; with `--reconcile` `1` on any difference between the export and the booked fills |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss sales --dry-run` |

### `vss newsdrop`

The news-drop screen, shadow mode: large names that fell hard on their own news.

> THE NEWS-DROP SCREEN, SHADOW MODE (reference/NEWS-DROP-DESIGN): large S&P 500 and Stockholm names down 10% in five days (or 5% in one) against their index, sorted by the company's own filings in the window. Writes data/newsdrop/; one ntfy message only when something survives the sorting; never writes the watchlist.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--asof YYYY-MM-DD` | the close to read (default: today) |
| `--limit LIMIT` | read only the first N names (a smoke run) |
| `--no-notify` | write the files but POST nothing to ntfy |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the S&P 500 and Stockholm large-cap lists under `config/universe/` |
| **Writes** | `data/newsdrop/`; `reports/NEWSDROP-<date>.md`. Never the watchlist (shadow mode) |
| **Network** | Yahoo (prices); EDGAR and the Nordic feed (the company's own filings in the window); a news RSS search; ntfy |
| **Sends** | to `NTFY_TOPIC`: one message, only when a name survives the sorting. `--no-notify` sends nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` |
| **Changes nothing** | none -- `--no-notify` still writes its files |

### `vss checkin`

The dead man's switch: is a completed run on record, are the timers alive?.

> THE DEAD MAN'S SWITCH's independent leg: is a completed run on record, and are the timers still enabled? Silence when healthy.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--no-send` | print the findings, POST nothing |
| `--hours N` | how many hours without a completed nightly run counts as a gap (default: 72) |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `data/vss.sqlite` (the completed runs); the user-level systemd timers (enabled, active) |
| **Writes** | nothing |
| **Network** | ntfy, and only when something is wrong |
| **Sends** | to `NTFY_TOPIC`: no completed nightly run within the window, or a timer not enabled and active. Silence when healthy |
| **Exit codes** | `0` always -- a finding is not an error; a non-zero exit means the check-in itself is broken |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss checkin --no-send` |

### `vss queue`

Every valued name against its lines; read each new report; send only a change.

> THE QUEUE (config/queue.yaml): every valued name against its buy, look and sell lines, its gate date and its new reports; one ntfy message when something CHANGED; writes reports/QUEUE-&lt;date&gt;.md and data/queue_state.json, never the watchlist.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--asof YYYY-MM-DD` | the day to judge (default: today) |
| `--no-notify` | write the report and the state, POST nothing |

| `--dry-run` | print the report; write no report file and no state, POST nothing. A NEW report found for a name is still fetched and read into data/autoread/ |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/queue.yaml`; `config/watchlist.yaml`; `data/queue_state.json`; `data/outlook_state.json` |
| **Writes** | `reports/QUEUE-<date>.md`; `data/queue_state.json`; `data/outlook_state.json`; `data/autoread/` (each new report and its reading); `reports/HUVUDLISTA.md`. Never the watchlist and never `config/queue.yaml` |
| **Network** | Yahoo (prices, quarterly statements); EDGAR and the Nordic / Oslo feeds (new reports); a news RSS search (headlines); OpenRouter (the reading); ntfy |
| **Sends** | to `NTFY_TOPIC`, one message and only on a CHANGE: `UNDER MBP`, `TITTA`, `SÄLJ`, `SPÄRR`, `UTSIKT`, `RÄTTELSE`, `RAPPORTKONTROLL FELADE`; weekly while it lasts: `STORLEK` and `SÄLJ EJ UTFÖRD` |
| **Exit codes** | `0` |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss queue --dry-run` writes no report and no state and sends nothing. One thing it still does: a NEW report found for a name is fetched into `data/autoread/` and read (the model is called), and the real run will read it again |

### `vss reference-figures`

Fetch the issuer's own free cash flow and net debt as reference figures (E103).

> E103: fetch the issuer's OWN free cash flow and net debt for E101's construction checks, and enter them UNVERIFIED. They are REFERENCE figures -- compared against a valuation, never used to build one -- which is why no read-back is required first and why the section 5 gate refuses if one is ever wired into a basis.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker TICKER` | one name (default: every store) |
| `--confirm` | E104: re-extract every DISAGREEING check's comparator on a narrow excerpt around the line the first pass quoted, and withdraw any figure two independent readings do not agree on. A figure the owner has VERIFIED is never re-read |
| `--write` | write what was obtained into the store (UNVERIFIED). Without it, nothing is written and the plan is printed |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the stores under `config/manual/` |
| **Writes** | nothing without `--write`. With it: the issuer's own free cash flow and net debt into the store as UNVERIFIED REFERENCE figures; `--confirm --write` withdraws a figure two readings do not agree on |
| **Network** | EDGAR; OpenRouter |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` |
| **Changes nothing** | without `--write` (the plan is printed; the model is still called) |

### `vss briefing`

Assemble the research a reading stands on; no judgement, no value.

> E76's BRIEFING: the research a reading stands on, assembled from the filings on EDGAR plus web search where a filing cannot answer. RESEARCH AND NOT A VERDICT -- it carries no judgement, no growth rate and no fair value, and refuses itself if it does. The E76 reading stays the owner's.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | a ticker with a complete store (REQUIRED) |
| `--cik N` | override the CIK from the watchlist or the store |
| `--asof YYYY-MM-DD` | the date the briefing is dated and the twelve insider months are counted back from (default: today) |
| `--write` | write reports/BRIEFING-&lt;TICKER&gt;-&lt;date&gt;.md |
| `--no-web` | do not call out. The sections a filing cannot answer then say NOT FILLED, which is the honest answer and not a hole |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; the name's store |
| **Writes** | nothing without `--write`. With it: `reports/BRIEFING-<TICKER>-<date>.md` |
| **Network** | EDGAR; OpenRouter with web search unless `--no-web` |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` assembled; `2` no CIK, no complete store, or the briefing refused itself (it carried a judgement) |
| **Changes nothing** | without `--write` |

### `vss prepare`

Everything the machine can do before a review, ending in a readiness report.

> everything that can happen before the owner sits down to review a name, run by the machine, ending in a readiness report under reports/prepare/. Route, fetch, fill, compute, verification list, human-step context -- each an EXISTING path; where none exists the report says so. NEVER writes fv_base, tier, mbp, stop_price or status; never writes the watchlist; backs up before any write to config/manual/.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | one ticker from the watchlist (one of these is required: `--all-pipeline`) |
| `--all-pipeline` | every PIPELINE name on the watchlist (one of these is required: `--ticker X`) |
| `--dry-run` | route, list the manifest, compute and verify from what is on disk; fetch nothing from a feed, read nothing with a model, write nothing anywhere |
| `--force` | re-fill a store that is already on file and re-extract a period already entered. The file is backed up first and the VERIFIED figures being discarded are named (appendix.py's semantics) |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |
| `--manual-dir PATH` | read and write stores in an alternate directory |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/watchlist.yaml`; the stores; `sources/` |
| **Writes** | `reports/prepare/<TICKER>-<date>.{json,md}`; stores under `config/manual/` (backed up first); documents under `sources/`. Never the watchlist |
| **Network** | EDGAR; the Nordic feeds; OpenRouter |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` ready; `1` at least one name is blocked on a step the machine could not do |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss prepare --ticker X --dry-run` |

Value one name off its store: run record, strike document, before/after table.

> re-strike one name off its store on the record's PRE-REGISTERED growth view, write the run record and the strike doc, and print the before/after table -- fv_base, bear, bull, the MBP with the tier on both sides, g*, and which leg moved. One front door for what the dated scripts in tools/ do. It NEVER writes the watchlist: fv_base, tier, mbp, stop_price and status stay the owner's act.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ticker X` | the name to strike; it needs a store and a registered growth view (REQUIRED) |

| `--dry-run` | print the table and the document; write nothing |
| `--stamp TEXT` | the record's filename stamp (default: the as-of date). Use it where a ruling names the pass, e.g. 2026-09-19-e117 |
| `--note TEXT` | one sentence into the record's notes and the document's header |
| `--ignore-gate` | strike although the section 5 gate REFUSES (E21). The refusal is printed, written into the record's notes and into the strike doc |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |
| `--manual-dir PATH` | read stores from an alternate directory |
| `--records-dir PATH` | read and write run records elsewhere |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the store; the watchlist entry's registered `growth:` view; `config/history/<TICKER>.yaml`; the previous run record; `data/vss.sqlite` (the tier in force, for the memo column) |
| **Writes** | `reference/run-records/<TICKER>-<stamp>.json` and `reference/<TICKER>-STRIKE-<stamp>.md`. Never the watchlist: `fv_base`, `tier`, `mbp`, `stop_price` and `status` stay the owner's act |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` struck; `2` REFUSED, and nothing was written: no store, no registered growth view, an events ledger dated more than seven days ago (E140(4): search the news and the filings again, then date it), or the section 5 gate refuses and `--ignore-gate` was not given |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss strike --ticker X --dry-run` |

### `vss history`

Build, check or print the issuer's multi-year history (E143).

### `vss review`

Validate or record a review session's file; print the review schema.

> the review session's record: validate a reference/reviews/&lt;TICKER&gt;/&lt;date&gt;.yaml against the review's step list and E28's ordering, or record one -- the owner's note appended verbatim to the watchlist entry (backup first) and the growth view registered where the code keeps growth views. NEVER writes status, fv_base, tier, mbp or stop_price; the file is re-read after the write and restored if anything else moved.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--validate PATH` | check the review file and print every refusal; writes nothing (one of these is required: `--record PATH`, `--schema`) |
| `--record PATH` | validate, then append the note and register the view (one of these is required: `--validate PATH`, `--schema`) |
| `--schema` | print config/review/SCHEMA.md as the code defines it (one of these is required: `--validate PATH`, `--record PATH`) |
| `--dry-run` | with --record: validate and say what would be written, write nothing |
| `--config PATH` | use an alternate watchlist |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | the review file under `reference/reviews/<TICKER>/`; `config/watchlist.yaml` |
| **Writes** | nothing with `--validate` or `--schema`. With `--record`: the owner's note appended verbatim to the entry's `notes` (backup first) and the growth view registered; the file is re-read afterwards and restored if anything else moved. Never `status`, `fv_base`, `tier`, `mbp` or `stop_price` |
| **Network** | none |
| **Sends** | nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0` valid (or recorded); `2` a refusal -- every one is printed |
| **Changes nothing** | `vss review --validate <file>`; `--schema`; `--record <file> --dry-run` |

### `vss screen`

The screener: universe, snapshot, filters, seeded order; `--weekly` for the chain.

> THE SCREENER: build the universe, snapshot its prices, run the exclusion list, the staleness gate and the coarse quality filter, and list what is left in a seeded order (E167). One step flag per call, or --weekly for the whole chain. Writes the watchlist only with --rank --write-pipeline.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--weekly` | E93: the WHOLE chain unattended -- snapshot, fundamentals, rank -- then store the ranked order, compare it with the previous stored run, write reports/SCREEN-&lt;date&gt;.md and post a pointer if anything crossed the top 10. NEVER writes the watchlist and NEVER enters a name as PIPELINE: that stamps dd_at_entry and freezes Gate 1 (E12), which a clock may not do |
| `--keep N` | with --weekly: how many price snapshots to keep (default: 4). Every ranking is kept forever whatever this says |
| `--no-notify` | with --weekly: compute and report, POST nothing |
| `--universe-report` | what the committed universe lists contain: count per market, count excluded per reason, count without a valid yahoo mapping |
| `--snapshot-only` | fetch prices for the whole universe and store them, filtering nothing |
| `--filter1` | run the exclusion list and the staleness gate against a stored snapshot (no drawdown band since E161, no 12-month-return test since E168). Fetches nothing |
| `--fundamentals` | fetch fundamentals for the survivors of filter 1, one ticker at a time, and store them beside the price snapshot |
| `--filter2` | run the whole chain against stored data: step 0, filter 1, then coarse quality. Fetches nothing |
| `--rank` | the whole chain, then the names that passed in a seeded random order with one fixed seed (E167). The old ranking key's two legs are still written to ranking.csv as information; they order nothing. Fetches only the exchange rates it needs |
| `--sec-shadow` | with --rank: SHADOW-check each US survivor's EBIT and total assets against SEC companyfacts clipped to --asof (column sec_check; the ranking stays on the vendor) |
| `--fx-from-manifest PATH` | with --rank: replay the exchange rates recorded in a stored ranking-manifest.json instead of fetching. Without it the rates are the LATEST close whatever --asof says, so a re-run of an old date is auditable but NOT reproducible. A pair the manifest does not carry fails and is named; it is never quietly fetched |
| `--write-pipeline` | with --rank: enter the top names in config/watchlist.yaml as PIPELINE. Backs the file up first and never touches an existing entry. No mbp, no fv_base, no tier |
| `--top N` | how many names --write-pipeline enters, from the top of the seeded order of names with both legs readable (default: 5) |
| `--dry-run` | with --write-pipeline: show what would be written, write nothing |
| `--from-snapshot YYYY-MM-DD` | which stored snapshot to read (default: the oldest one dated on or after --asof) |
| `--exclusions PATH` | use an alternate exclusion list instead of config/screener_exclusions.csv |
| `--asof YYYY-MM-DD` | the session to snapshot. Rows dated after it are DROPPED, so a re-run reproduces that day rather than today (default: today) |
| `--tier A|B|C` | which tier to load; repeatable (default: A) |
| `--universe-dir PATH` | use an alternate universe directory instead of config/universe |
| `--snapshot-root PATH` | where snapshots are written (default: data/screener_snapshots) |
| `--runs-root PATH` | where filter1-candidates.csv, ranking.csv and the ranking manifest are written (default: data/screener_runs). A comparison run MUST set this: pointing only --snapshot-root at a scratch directory leaves the run writing its ranking over the real one for that date, which happened on 2026-08-31 to the 2026-08-29 file |
| `--batch-size N` | tickers per price request (default: 50) |
| `--limit N` | stop after N instruments -- a smoke test, never a real run |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | `config/universe/`; `config/screener_exclusions.csv`; `config/screener_filter2.yaml`; the stored snapshots |
| **Writes** | `data/screener_snapshots/<asof>/`; `data/screener_runs/<asof>/` (`filter1-candidates.csv`, `ranking.csv`, `ranking-manifest.json`); with `--weekly` also `reports/SCREEN-<date>.md` and the ranked order in `data/vss.sqlite`. ONLY `--rank --write-pipeline` writes `config/watchlist.yaml`: new PIPELINE entries, backup first, never an existing entry |
| **Network** | Yahoo (prices, fundamentals, exchange rates); `data.sec.gov` with `--sec-shadow` and `--weekly`; ntfy with `--weekly` |
| **Sends** | `--weekly` posts a pointer to `NTFY_TOPIC` when the first ten changed; `--no-notify` sends nothing |
| **Exit codes** | `0`; `2` a universe file is malformed, no step flag was given, or the newest stored snapshot is older than `--asof` |
| **Changes nothing** | `--universe-report`, `--filter1` and `--filter2` fetch nothing and write only under `data/screener_runs/`; `--write-pipeline --dry-run` shows what would be entered |

## The backtests

Modules under `tools/backtest/` and `tools/newsdrop/`, run as `.venv/bin/python -m tools.backtest.<name>`. They read licensed vendor data that you fetch under your own licence (`tools/fetch_eodhd.py`); none of it, and nothing computed from it, is in the repository. Every run is registered in `reference/backtest/ATTEMPTS.md` before it starts (E164).

| Module | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools.backtest.a1_guard` | TEST A1 (a) and (b) (ATTEMPTS #15): every return the level-break guard changed, where the row sat in the rankings, and whether the guard brought survivorship back |
| `tools.backtest.a23_growth` | ATTEMPTS #23 (pre-registered 2026-11-08, before any run): does E144's derived growth OVERESTIMATE the growth later realised? |
| `tools.backtest.a24_deciles` | ATTEMPTS #24 (pre-registered 2026-11-08, before any run): the hard kills 4.2.1 / 4.2.2 / 4.2.7 as continuous signals, and the screener's ordering candidates, by decile ... |
| `tools.backtest.a25_filters` | ATTEMPTS #25 (pre-registered 2026-11-09, before any run): every mechanical filter still in the method and never tested, as IN against OUT, in one run |
| `tools.backtest.a3_kills` | TEST A3 (ATTEMPTS #17): the hard-kill thresholds |
| `tools.backtest.a5_jkp` | TEST A5 (ATTEMPTS #19): our best-minus-worst spreads against the JKP factors (Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen 2023, jkpfactors.com, CC BY-NC 4.0) |
| `tools.backtest.a6_funds` | TEST A6 re-run (ATTEMPTS #20b): our best fifths against real value funds, in SEK, before and after costs |
| `tools.backtest.a7_ablation` | TEST A7 (ATTEMPTS #21): ablation of the method's chain, and competitors |
| `tools.backtest.band_momentum` | TEST 3 (wrez-devour, pre-registered in reference/backtest/ATTEMPTS.md #12): Gate 1's 15-50% band in the NORDICS, and a 12-1 momentum filter in both |
| `tools.backtest.benchmarks` | TEST A2 (ATTEMPTS #16): the best and worst fifths against several benchmarks, and Ken French's value portfolios over the same windows |
| `tools.backtest.concentration` | TEST 2 (wrez-devour, pre-registered in reference/backtest/ATTEMPTS.md #11): concentration -- equal-weight portfolios of 3, 5, 10, 20 names |
| `tools.backtest.confirm_nordic` | The pre-registered evaluation of the Nordic backtest (reference/backtest/PREREG-NORDIC-CONFIRM-2026-11-07.md) |
| `tools.backtest.devour` | Shared engine for the wrez-devour tests of November 2026 (stops, concentration, the band / momentum filter, F-score and accruals) |
| `tools.backtest.eodhd_reprice` | Re-price the full run with EODHD prices -- delisted companies included |
| `tools.backtest.fscore_accruals` | TEST 4 (wrez-devour, pre-registered in reference/backtest/ATTEMPTS.md #13): Piotroski's F-score and Sloan's accruals from point-in-time fundamentals |
| `tools.backtest.fundsig` | Round 2 signals (ATTEMPTS #17, #19, #21): per valued row, from the facts visible on the test day |
| `tools.backtest.measure` | The measure (backtest design, step 6), on the rows `run` wrote |
| `tools.backtest.measure_key` | The LIVE screener's ranking key and drawdown band, measured on the US run |
| `tools.backtest.method` | The method's core on one name and one date, without the engine's store (backtest path 1, owner 2026-10-29) |
| `tools.backtest.method_pilot` | Path 1's pilot: the method's core (`method`) on the step-4 draw |
| `tools.backtest.nolb` | TEST A1 (round 2, ATTEMPTS #15): the same rows with and without the level-break guard (review 2026-11-08 M2, e816c76) |
| `tools.backtest.nordic` | The method's core on NORDIC companies, from EODHD (private data) |

## Modules

Every module under `vss/`, with the opening of its own docstring. `rules.py` and `valuation.py` are pure: no I/O and no clock, `as_of` is always passed in. `runner.py` holds the nightly run's I/O; `pipeline.py` and `review.py` are the only modules that write the watchlist.

| Module | What it is |
|---|---|
| `vss/__main__.py` | CLI entrypoint: ``python -m vss run`` |
| `vss/appendix.py` | A figures appendix, read through a committed cell-to-field map |
| `vss/autoread.py` | `vss watch --read` -- read each filing the SEC arm passed, IN SHADOW |
| `vss/briefing.py` | E76's BRIEFING: the research a reading stands on, assembled automatically |
| `vss/calendars.py` | Exchange calendars for the staleness gate (FRAMEWORK-EDITS E47 / C3) |
| `vss/catalyst.py` | Gate 1's catalyst limb: the DATED FACTS a reader needs, and nothing more |
| `vss/cfrecon.py` | E140(1)'s working capital, read off the cash flow statement ITSELF and tied to the filer's own printed operating cash flow (data rule, E164; decided by the owner ... |
| `vss/config.py` | Watchlist loading and validation |
| `vss/doctor.py` | `vss doctor` -- is this machine able to run vss? Read-only |
| `vss/draft.py` | `vss manual --merge-draft`: a pre-fill DRAFT into the live store |
| `vss/earnings.py` | `vss earnings` -- read a primary source and flag FRAMEWORK 4.2 trips |
| `vss/env.py` | Operational settings: the ENVIRONMENT first, then `~/.config/vss/vss.env` |
| `vss/esef.py` | Facts out of ONE ESEF report package, in the companyfacts API's shape |
| `vss/events.py` | E140(3)-(4) and E140.1(3): the EVENTS LEDGER a strike stands on |
| `vss/extract.py` | LLM figure extraction from a primary source (OpenRouter) |
| `vss/fetch.py` | Daily OHLCV retrieval with an on-disk cache (SCOPE 2) |

| `vss/fundamentals.py` | Fundamentals retrieval for the survivors of filter 1 (screener step 3) |
| `vss/fx.py` | Exchange rates for the ranking key (FRAMEWORK-EDITS E5(b), kept by E6) |
| `vss/heartbeat.py` | THE DEAD MAN'S SWITCH: a run that does not happen must not look like a quiet one |
| `vss/history.py` | The issuer's own multi-year history, and what E142-E145 derive from it |

## Timers

User-level systemd units under `deploy/`, read off the files. Times are the machine's local time unless the expression says UTC. **Failure hook** says whether the service names `vss-failure@.service` as its `OnFailure=`, which posts to `NTFY_TOPIC` that the unit failed. `vss-overview.service` has no timer: it serves `reports/OVERVIEW.html` on loopback.

| Timer | When (`OnCalendar`) | Runs | Failure hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vss-checkin.timer` | `*-*-* 09:30:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss checkin` | yes |
| `vss-eodhd-reminder.timer` | `*-04-15 09:00:00` | `.venv/bin/python -c "from vss.watch import post_ntfy; print(post_ntfy(['Dags för årets EODHD-...` | no |
| `vss-eodhd.timer` | `*-*-* 01:30:00 UTC` | `.venv/bin/python tools/fetch_eodhd.py --budget 90000 --reserve 10000`<br>then `.venv/bin/python tools/eodhd_pit.py --build` | yes |
| `vss-mfn.timer` | `*-*-* 22:40:00` | `.venv/bin/python tools/fetch_mfn.py --queue --days 45`<br>then `.venv/bin/python tools/cross_verify.py --all --apply` | yes |
| `vss-newsdrop.timer` | `Mon..Fri *-*-* 23:00:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss newsdrop` | yes |
| `vss-nordic-screen.timer` | `Sat *-*-* 08:00:00` | `.venv/bin/python tools/nordic_screen.py --notify` | yes |
| `vss-queue.timer` | `Mon..Fri *-*-* 22:50:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss queue` | yes |
| `vss-screen.timer` | `Sat *-*-* 08:00:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss screen --weekly --tier A --tier B` | yes |
| `vss-watch.timer` | `*-*-* 13:00:00; *-*-* 23:30:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss watch --read` | yes |
| `vss.timer` | `*-*-* 22:30:00` | `.venv/bin/python -m vss run`<br>then `deploy/vss-ping-healthcheck.sh` | yes |

## Environment variables

Read from the environment first, then from `~/.config/vss/vss.env` (`vss/env.py`) -- the file the systemd units name in `EnvironmentFile=`. The environment wins; the file is never written, logged or printed.

| Variable | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VSS_SEC_CONTACT` | `xbrl`, `history --xbrl`, `watch`, `queue`, `briefing`, `refresh`, `prepare`, `newsdrop`, `tools/warren.py` | The contact address SEC asks every automated caller to declare, e.g. `yourtool/1.0 (you@example.com)`. Without it SEC is not called |
| `VSS_OPENROUTER_KEY` | `earnings`, `pdfdraft`, `briefing`, `reference-figures`, `prepare`, `refresh`, `watch --read`, `queue`, `tools/cross_verify.py` | The model key. Never in the repository. Without it a reading says so and nothing is guessed |
| `VSS_OPENROUTER_MODEL` | the same | Optional: the model id. Defaults to the one named in `vss/extract.py` |
| `NTFY_TOPIC` | `run`, `queue`, `checkin`, `newsdrop`, `screen --weekly`, `tools/nordic_screen.py --notify` | Where pointers are POSTed. A bare topic name is completed to `https://ntfy.sh/<topic>`; a full URL is used as given. Unset is silence, not an error. Outbound only |
| `VSS_NTFY_URL` | `watch` | `vss watch`'s own topic URL, separate on purpose: a disclosure alert is not a refresh pointer |
| `HEALTHCHECK_URL` | `deploy/vss-ping-healthcheck.sh` | A healthchecks.io ping URL, fetched only after a nightly run that SUCCEEDED: the one alarm a powered-off machine can still raise |
| `EODHD_API_KEY` | `tools/fetch_eodhd.py`, `tools/nordic_screen.py` | Your own EODHD licence, in `~/.config/eodhd/env` (mode 600). Only the Nordic screen and the backtests need it |
| `BT_WORKERS` | `tools/backtest/` | Optional: how many processes a backtest uses |

## Files

TRACKED means in git. Everything under `data/` and `reports/` is gitignored and regenerable.

| Path | Written by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `config/watchlist.yaml` | the owner by hand; `screen --rank --write-pipeline` (new PIPELINE entries); `review --record` (a note) | TRACKED. One entry per name: status, `fv_base`, `tier`, notes, hand-entered quarters. Every field is manual; `mbp` is computed and may not be written |
| `config/queue.yaml` | `tools/build_queue.py --write`; hand fields by the owner | TRACKED. Every valued name with bear / base / bull, its kind (`strike`, `machine`, `rough`), tier, gate and the hand fields `sell_at`, `look_at`, `note`, `exit_pending`, `override`; `portfolio_sek` for the 6 % size ceiling |
| `config/manual/<TICKER>.yaml` | `xbrl --annual --write`, `appendix --write`, `manual --merge-draft`, `refresh`, `prepare`, by hand | TRACKED. The store: every figure with its source, page and status (`UNVERIFIED` / `VERIFIED`) |
| `config/manual/drafts/` | `esef --draft`, `pdfdraft --write` | TRACKED. Machine pre-fills, every figure UNVERIFIED; never read as the store |
| `config/history/<TICKER>.yaml` | `history --xbrl --write`, `history --esef --write`, by hand | TRACKED. The issuer's multi-year history E142-E145 read |
| `config/shadow_book.csv` | by hand | TRACKED. One row per refusal, nine columns |
| `config/sales_reconciled.yaml` | `sales --reconcile` | TRACKED. The booked fills matched against the account export (E165) |
| `config/universe/` | `tools/build_universe.py` | TRACKED. Static, dated constituent lists; never fetched at run time |
| `reference/run-records/` | `strike` | TRACKED. Every input and every choice of a valuation; a value with no record is not a value |
| `reference/<TICKER>-STRIKE-<stamp>.md` | `strike` | TRACKED. The strike document: the before/after table and the waterfall |
| `reference/reviews/<TICKER>/` | the `/review` session | TRACKED. One review file per session, validated by `review --validate` |
| `sources/` | `nordic --download`, `tools/fetch_mfn.py`, `prepare` | The documents themselves are gitignored (large, re-downloadable); `sources/manifest.json` is TRACKED: URL, SHA-256, bytes and fetch time per file |
| `reports/<date>.md` | `run` | The nightly report |
| `reports/OVERVIEW.html` | `run` (full runs), `overview` | The read-only page: one file, no script |
| `reports/QUEUE-<date>.md` | `queue` | The night's queue table |
| `reports/HUVUDLISTA.md` | `queue`, `tools/master_list.py` | The master list: every company looked at, in five groups |
| `reports/SCREEN-<date>.md` | `screen --weekly` | The weekly screen |
| `reports/NEWSDROP-<date>.md` | `newsdrop` | The news-drop screen (shadow) |
| `reports/SALES-RECORD-<date>.md` | `sales` | Every closed position against the indices |
| `reports/SHADOW-BOOK-<date>.md` | `shadow` | Every refusal against the indices |
| `reports/REFRESH-<TICKER>-<date>.md` | `refresh` | What a report-date refresh fetched and left for the owner |
| `reports/BRIEFING-<TICKER>-<date>.md` | `briefing --write` | Research for a reading; carries no judgement |
| `reports/prepare/` | `prepare` | Readiness reports, json and md |
| `data/vss.sqlite` | `run`, `earnings`, `screen --weekly`, `backfill-vendor-strings`, `tools/seed_fields_history.py` | Tables `runs`, `run_metrics` (one row per ticker per run), `earnings_runs`, the stored rankings, the vendor strings, `fundamentals_fields_history`. New columns arrive by a migration on connect |
| `data/cache/` | `run`, `sales`, `shadow` | Daily prices per ticker, CSV plus a JSON sidecar |
| `data/queue_state.json` | `queue` | Which zone each name was in last night, so a change is said once; the last closes |
| `data/outlook_state.json` | `queue` | Each name's last four-quarter value and the reports and headlines already handled |
| `data/autoread/` | `queue`, `watch --read` | Every fetched report and its reading (two runs, compared). Shadow: nothing here is sent |
| `data/watch_state.json` | `watch` | The disclosure cursor per name |
| `data/refresh_state.json` | `refresh` | What each refresh fetched and what waits for the owner |
| `data/pricewatch_state.json` | `run` | The ranked watch's crossings (E97), so each is said once |
| `data/block_push_state.json` | `run` | Whether last night's blocked-level push went, and each name's streak |
| `data/screener_snapshots/<asof>/` | `screen` | Raw daily OHLCV for the whole universe, plus `fundamentals.sqlite` |
| `data/screener_runs/<asof>/` | `screen` | `filter1-candidates.csv`, `ranking.csv`, `ranking-manifest.json` |
| `data/sec-cache/` | `screen --rank --sec-shadow`, `screen --weekly` | SEC companyfacts as fetched |
| `data/newsdrop/` | `newsdrop` | The screen's own files |
| `data/cross-verify/` | `tools/cross_verify.py` | Cached second readings |
| `data/eodhd/` | `tools/fetch_eodhd.py`, `tools/eodhd_pit.py` | Licensed vendor data under your own licence; never published |
